lines: +**Retrying `version` finishes when its emitted decision is inside the workspace.** A run that wrote `--emit-decision` or `--emit-preview` into `.changeset` and was then interrupted no longer refuses its own retry with `E340`.
+- A hand edit to that file after the interruption is still refused.
+**Shorter release configuration.** List your build targets once and let Callisto name each asset, and drop `forge-repository`.

+- How to adopt it: replace repeated `[[release.artifact]]` blocks for the product with `targets = [...]` and `asset-name = "tool-{target}.tar.gz"` under `[release]`. Keep `[[release.artifact]]` for another package's artifact or an irregular name such as a Windows `.zip`.
+- `forge-repository` is optional: Callisto uses the `origin` GitHub repository, which every release already required it to equal.
+- `callisto init` now writes `targets` and one `asset-name` template, named after the single binary or after the package when it has several.
+- Limits: `{target}` is the only placeholder. A target named by both `targets` and a `[[release.artifact]]` of the product is E197.
+**Breaking:** `callisto init` no longer asks for or accepts `--forge-repository`.
+**Package directories with unusual names release correctly.** A package directory named with `*`, `?` or leading spaces is now read as exactly that directory.
+- Commit inference and the version commit no longer pick up a sibling such as `packages/odd-other` for a package in `packages/odd*`.
+- A commit message containing the U+001E control character no longer stops inference with `E026`.
+- Resuming an interrupted `version` run in a workspace directory with leading or trailing spaces resumes that workspace, not a similarly named sibling.
+**Generated release workflows publish only what a credential-free job built.** Package scripts, build backends and crate builds no longer run in the job that holds your registry tokens.

+- The publish job uploads exactly the Python files and npm tarballs a job without credentials built and sealed, and publishes crates with `cargo publish --no-verify` after that job compiled every crate of the release, one `cargo package --locked` call per Cargo workspace, including a workspace under a directory such as `native/` with no root manifest.

+- The simple workflow now has `version-pr`, `package` and `execute` jobs, and the build-matrix workflow gains `attest`, `package-cargo` and `pack-npm` jobs, so only `execute` holds secrets and only the attestation job holds an OIDC token without checking out your code.
+- npm packages are packed by their workspace's own package manager, so `workspace:` and `catalog:` ranges are rewritten in the published tarball.
+- A local `callisto release` still verifies crates and packs in place, with registry credentials withheld from the build.

+**Breaking:** npm publishes now run `npm publish <tarball> --ignore-scripts`. The `prepublishOnly`, `publish` and `postpublish` hooks no longer run, and `prepack` and `prepare` run in the pack job, which has no registry credentials. The simple workflow now publishes only when a push adds or changes the release decision file, not whenever an untagged version is merged. A release whose npm or PyPI publish is not sealed in the artifact manifest now fails with E306 before anything is published.

+**Breaking:** `npm publish <tarball>` does not read a registry set in `.yarnrc.yml` or `bunfig.toml`. A yarn workspace whose `.yarnrc.yml` sets `npmPublishRegistry` or `npmRegistryServer` (at the top level or under `npmScopes`), or a bun workspace whose `bunfig.toml` sets a registry, now fails with E168 before anything is published, and Yarn and Bun token settings are not used either.

+**Action:** Yarn and Bun users: move the registry to `publishConfig.registry` in your package's `package.json`, or to `.npmrc`, and keep the publish token in `NPM_TOKEN`. Everyone: delete `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml` and regenerate it with `callisto init --workflow`, then move work that must run at publish time from `prepublishOnly`, `publish` or `postpublish` into `prepack` or a step of your own after `execute`.

The generated workflow keeps a release PR current. Merging that PR to the protected default branch authorizes publication; Callisto adds no approval step. Require reviews and CI checks in branch protection. A CODEOWNERS file alone does not enforce review.

The action's `version-pr` mode updates the PR; `release` runs `callisto release` for a hand-written local workflow, and `execute` runs `callisto release execute` on the intent and files a credential-free job prepared. Generated workflows use plan/build/execute (build-matrix) or package/execute (simple). See the [action inputs](../.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml).

Only `execute` receives registry credentials or an OIDC token for publishing. Keep `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, and `TWINE_PASSWORD` out of workflow scope, planning, build, pack and attestation jobs, and action inputs. The attestation job holds `id-token: write`, so it has no checkout and runs no command.

After a failed committed-decision CI release, "Re-run failed jobs" adopts completed effects and performs the rest. A green workflow alone is not proof of publication: check the receipt and providers.

The action's `version-pr` mode updates the PR; `release` runs `callisto release` for a hand-written local workflow, and `execute` runs `callisto release execute` on the intent and files a credential-free job prepared. Generated workflows use plan/build/execute (build-matrix) or package/execute (simple). See the [action inputs](../.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml).

Only `execute` receives registry credentials or an OIDC token for publishing. Keep `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, and `TWINE_PASSWORD` out of workflow scope, planning, build, pack and attestation jobs, and action inputs. The attestation job holds `id-token: write`, so it has no checkout and runs no command.

If a stale release PR whose changesets were already consumed on `main` was merged anyway, the release fails with [E165](errors.md) because the changesets the merge deleted are not the ones its decision recorded, and every later push to `main` retries it.
